subject: NovaSys: sustained error spike and throughput plateau — leadership command cadence
messages:
From: Danielle Park <ops@novasys.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Ethan Ross <procurement@novasys.com>, Maya Li <ceo@novasys.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Service impact: increased 5xx and throughput ceiling observed

Aditya —

We started seeing a sustained increase in 5xx errors across our QA and prod clusters starting ~08:45 PT. Concurrently, requests that previously scaled linearly now appear to cap at ~60rps and queue up, increasing tail latency. This is affecting our checkout flow and we are seeing ~3% revenue impact on the last hour.

I've attached the incident log and a short throughput graph. Key notes:
- Errors are predominantly 503/504 from the inference endpoint (model: open-7b-v2).
- Error spike correlates with a change in request pattern from a long-tail bot campaign starting ~08:30.
- We've restarted a small subset of pods to reduce error rate but the throughput ceiling persists.

Can Redwood stand up a command-level bridge and provide an initial assessment and ETA for mitigation? Senior leadership is on standby.

Attachments: incident_log_0818.txt, throughput_graph_0818.png

—Danielle Park
Director, Site Reliability
NovaSys

- Markus to lead performance triage (kernel/batching/queueing).
- Monica to own customer comms and exec updates.
- Sean to review SLA posture and propose interim credits.

Ask from NovaSys: if you can share 3 request IDs that produced 503/504 responses and a short capture of the traffic spike (sample of user-agents and 1-minute qps) that will speed root cause analysis.

We will provide a 1-hour interim update and escalate to leadership if we see customer-visible error rate >1% after the first mitigation.

Attachments: copying your incident_log_0818.txt for the bridge.

On it. Quick assignments for the 10:30 bridge:

- Monica: prepare an external note for NovaSys execs summarizing a 3-point plan and projected time to stabilization. Keep tone factual and set expectations (we'll avoid overpromising).

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service impact: increased 5xx and throughput ceiling observed

Status update from triage (13:45 PT):
- Reproduced the plateau in our staging infra when replaying the same request mix NovaSys sent. Root cause hypothesis: a shift in request length distribution exposed a batching boundary bug that causes oversized batches to be rejected by the runtime kernel, leading to cascading queue growth and 503s when the request queue times out.
- Evidence: CPU traces show a sudden spike in kernel scheduling latency when sequence length > 2048 tokens and batch size grows beyond expected.

Short-term mitigation (now -> 3h):
1) Force per-request execution for a 10% traffic slice to break the batching aggregation (will reduce throughput on that slice but should lower 5xx).
2) Deploy a canary patch to the batching coordinator that caps batch size at a lower threshold (canary window 15 mins).
3) If the canary reduces errors, roll 50% traffic to the patched coordinator and monitor for 30 mins before full rollout.

Estimated RTO: 2–3 hours if canary proceeds without regressions. If we hit an unexpected failure, fallback is to route NovaSys traffic to the legacy quantized model variant (slightly higher latency, lower cost).

Attachments: throughput_graph_0818.png (annotated)

—Markus Klein
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Li <ceo@novasys.com>, Danielle Park <ops@novasys.com>, Ethan Ross <procurement@novasys.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: NovaSys stabilization update and next steps

Maya / Danielle / Ethan —

Thank you for your patience while we worked through the issue today. Summary of what happened and what we committed to:

1) Impact: a request-pattern shift triggered oversized batches in our serving runtime, producing cascading queue timeouts and a 5xx spike. NovaSys saw a throughput cap (~60rps) and increased tail latency across the checkout flow during the window 08:45–13:15 PT.

2) What we did:
- Mobilized an urgent leadership+engineering bridge at 10:30 PT.
- Deployed a canary to cap batch aggregation and forced a 10% single-request slice; observed a >70% drop in 5xx rate in the canary slice within 20 minutes.
- Gradually expanded the patch to 50% of NovaSys traffic with continued error-rate improvements.

3) Current status (16:20 PT):
- Error rate is back within an acceptable delta to baseline (0.4% vs pre-incident 0.1%).
- Throughput remains slightly below historic peak while we monitor for any regression; we expect to return to baseline in 6–8 hours as we complete the rollout and tune batching thresholds.

4) Customer-facing commitments:
- We will provide a formal RCA within 72 hours.
- If we cannot fully restore baseline throughput within 12 hours, Redwood will apply a service credit per section 4.2 of the SLA. Sean will follow up with the proposed credit amount.

5) Next steps for NovaSys & Redwood:
- Shared timeline: incremental rollout complete by 20:00 PT; final validation and closure by 02:00 PT tomorrow.
- Deliverables: patch notes, incremental monitoring dashboard (link below), and the RCA doc.

We take this seriously and will share the postmortem and action items tied to both code fixes and improved automated throttling thresholds. Monica will send the customer-friendly update and the CEO note in the next 30 minutes.

Links: INC-4921 bridge notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4921

Attachments: NOVASYS-SLA-commit.pdf (SLA clause excerpt)

—Aditya Rao
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
